question: Does a span-aware gap rule remove the fallback-rendering artefact found by the 2026-10-04 span test without losing sensitivity to real breaks?

inputs.byte_rule: every fiber re-downloaded and hash-matched; any failure is RUN FAILED

rules.old: step > gap_factor x the fiber's median non-zero step (current scroliq-fiber rule)
rules.span: step > gap_factor x the median non-zero step of its own control span when that span has >= min_span_steps non-zero steps; otherwise the fiber median; steps outside spans use the fiber median

planted_control.design: for each fiber and each span class (native, fallback) with an eligible span (>= min_span_steps non-zero steps), one eligible span is drawn at random and one interior non-zero step is stretched; all later points are translated so nothing else changes
planted_control.span_relative: primary: the planted step becomes plant_factor x that span's own median step (a step much longer than its neighbours)
planted_control.fiber_relative: descriptive: the planted step becomes plant_factor x the fiber median step (reported, not part of the decision)
planted_control.span_boundaries: computed once on the unmodified line

decision.rule: ADOPT iff span-relative planted recall of the span rule >= min_recall in native AND fallback spans, real fallback-span candidates under the span rule <= max_fallback_ratio x the old rule's, and native planted recall of the span rule >= the old rule's - max_native_recall_loss. INSUFFICIENT if fewer than min_planted_per_class planted breaks in either class. Otherwise KEEP.

disclosure: gap_factor, min_span_steps and plant_factor were chosen after the 2026-10-04 span test had reported that fallback spans render at a median 3.26x the fiber step. The frozen question is whether the span rule keeps sensitivity under planted breaks, not whether it reduces fallback candidates, which that result already makes likely.
interpretation_limits: Planted breaks are geometric stretches of real lines, not real annotation errors.
A fiber-relative break inside a sparsely rendered span is, by construction, hard for a span-aware rule; that trade-off is reported descriptively.
ADOPT changes no published number by itself; adopting the rule in scroliq-fiber is a separate, versioned change.
